solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Wretched dwelling inadequate for south coast location

indicators.note: inadequate means falling short, so the word for the dwelling loses its final letter

parts.note: a hovel is a wretched, squalid dwelling

explanation.surface: A miserable little house proves unfit for a seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inadequate' cuts the last letter from HOVEL. HOVE is a town on England's south coast, beside Brighton.
explanation.definitionFit: Proper name: a seaside town in East Sussex, joined to Brighton, on England's southern shore.

clue.text: Expression of frustration from little fellow very angry, upset

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the combined pieces are read bottom to top

parts.note: Tim is a short form of Timothy, a boy's name
mad means very angry

explanation.surface: A small man, livid and agitated, lets out a curse.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upset' turns the whole run upside down; 'from' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A mild oath, a softened form of 'damn it', blurted out when something goes wrong.

clue.text: Walk when there's no parking for vehicle

indicators.note: the walk word is to be taken without the letter for parking, so that letter goes

parts.note: to tramp is to walk heavily or a long way
P is the standard abbreviation for parking on road signs

explanation.surface: You have to go on foot if you can't park your car.
explanation.definitionFit: A tram is a passenger vehicle running on rails laid in the street.

clue.text: Army going up and down, one about to enter that old territory

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading the army letters from the bottom, so they turn round

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force

indicators.note: to enter means the one-and-about letters go inside the army letters taken downwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
C stands for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: Soldiers march up and down as someone approaches an ancient land.
explanation.walkthrough: The army word serves twice: once read upwards ('going up'), once downwards ('and down'), the second copy taking in 'one about' ('to enter'). The Territorial Army is Britain's reserve army.
explanation.definitionFit: Attica was the ancient Greek region around Athens, a territory of the classical world.

clue.text: Climbing mountain, something good for health according to one philosopher

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means going upwards, so the mountain word is read backwards

parts.note: an alp is a high mountain
a tonic is a restorative medicine or drink

explanation.surface: Mountain climbing is healthy, or so some philosopher says.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means following the ideas of Plato, the Greek thinker, so it fits 'in line with one sage'.

clue.text: Like pub landlords being detained?

definitions.meaning: publicans stand at the back of their counters, serving drinks

explanation.surface: Are publicans under arrest?
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means literally positioned at the back of a pub counter, and idiomatically imprisoned.

clue.text: Old fellow attending church in posh car is one given to extravagance

indicators.note: in means the old fellow and church go inside the letters for the posh car

parts.note: RR is Rolls-Royce, the luxury car
a man is a fellow
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: An elderly man goes to church in a Rolls, flaunting his wealth.
explanation.walkthrough: RR is Rolls-Royce, the British luxury car; CE is the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who romances spins fanciful, exaggerated tales, so is prone to extravagant invention.

clue.text: Most abrupt and ill-mannered person on trial

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above, so the cur comes before the trial

parts.note: a cur is a contemptible, surly person
a test is a trial

explanation.surface: A boorish defendant on trial is especially brusque.
explanation.definitionFit: Curt means brief to the point of rudeness; the superlative is the most brusque.

clue.text: What boatman uses in row across two lakes

indicators.note: across means the row stretches over the two lakes, so they sit within it

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
L is the abbreviation for lake, so two lakes give LL

explanation.surface: A rower pulls his oars across two lakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' looks like rowing, but here it is a line, a tier.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat is steered by the bar fixed to the rudder, which the helmsman holds.

clue.text: Our lot meeting when Dai et al. celebrate in German city

parts.note: we means us, our lot
Dai is a typical Welsh name, and the Welsh celebrate St David's Day on 1 March, written 1 MAR

explanation.surface: We join Welshmen at a party in a German town.
explanation.walkthrough: St David is the patron saint of Wales; his day, 1 March, gives I (one) and MAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Weimar is a city in Thuringia, home of Goethe and namesake of the 1919-33 republic.

clue.text: Support isn't accepted by chief

indicators.note: accepted by means taken in by, so the isn't word goes inside the chief word

parts.note: main means chief
ain't is a colloquial form of isn't

explanation.surface: Help is refused by the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: To support something is to keep it going or uphold it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Unfocused brat creates din, needing to be sorted out

indicators.note: sorted out means rearranged, so the letters of the three words are shuffled

explanation.surface: A distracted child makes a racket and needs taking in hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be sorted out' rearranges BRAT CREATES DIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A scatterbrained person is flighty and disorganised, unable to concentrate.

clue.text: Change of a climate is bringing disasters

indicators.note: a change of the words means altering their letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Climate change is causing catastrophes.
explanation.definitionFit: Calamities are catastrophes, grave misfortunes.

clue.text: Son hiding in Welsh location with lake and wood

indicators.note: hiding in means the son is tucked inside the Welsh place name

parts.note: Bala is a town in north Wales on Bala Lake (Llyn Tegid)

explanation.surface: A boy hides by a Welsh lake in a forest.
explanation.walkthrough: Bala is a small town in Gwynedd, north Wales, beside Wales's largest natural lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Balsa is a very light timber from a tropical American tree, used for models.

clue.text: One sort of learner embracing another in society

indicators.note: embracing means holding within, so the second learner sits inside the first

parts.note: a cub is a trainee, as a cub reporter or a junior Scout
another learner: L is the learner plate letter

explanation.surface: A novice takes another under his wing within an association.
explanation.walkthrough: L is from the plate a British learner driver displays.
explanation.definitionFit: A club is an association of members, a society.

clue.text: Experts sitting under massive trees

indicators.note: in a down clue, sitting under means placed below, so the experts follow

parts.note: bull- as in bull elephant suggests something large and massive
aces are experts

explanation.surface: Specialists rest in the shade of huge trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Bullaces are wild plum trees, bearing small sour fruit like damsons.

clue.text: High-level operator having renewed enthusiasm when returning

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the word is read from right to left

parts.note: relit, as of a passion fired up again

explanation.surface: A senior executive gets fired up again on coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High-level operator' suggests a senior manager, but means a worker up on the roof.
explanation.definitionFit: A roofer laying tiles works high up on buildings, a jokey sense of operating at height.

clue.text: Idolised revolutionary always getting captured

indicators.note: getting captured means the always word is held inside the revolutionary word

parts.note: red means a revolutionary communist
ever means always

explanation.surface: A rebel hero, worshipped forever, is finally caught.
explanation.definitionFit: To be idolised is to be held in deep respect, venerated.

clue.text: Loud noise lacking in our reticent person

indicators.note: lacking means without, so the word our is removed from the noise word

parts.note: clamour is a loud noise, an uproar

explanation.surface: Our quiet friend makes no racket.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who clams up keeps silent, so a closed, quiet person is likened to a shellfish.

clue.text: Such a vile man — it could be me!

definitions.text: Such a vile man — it could be me!

indicators.note: could be means the letters might form something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A confession that the speaker might be an odious type of man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' rearranges SUCH A VILE MAN IT; the whole clue also describes the answer, a man who might admit 'it could be me'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sexist man who thinks men superior to women is a vile man by modern lights.

clue.text: This person's wearing dear Parisian robe

indicators.note: wearing means being clothed in, so the person's word sits inside the French word

parts.note: cher is French for dear
I'm is the setter speaking of himself: this person is

explanation.surface: I dress myself in a fine French gown.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimer, or chimere, is the loose sleeveless gown worn by Anglican bishops.

clue.text: Bits of food Diana chose, wasting some

indicators.note: wasting some means discarding the outer letters, leaving a run inside the two words

explanation.surface: Diana picked some snacks but threw part away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wasting some' drops DIA and E from DIANA CHOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Tortilla chips served with toppings, eaten as snack pieces.

clue.text: Very angry chant when side goes in

indicators.note: goes in means the side word is placed inside the chant word

parts.note: to sing is to chant
a team is a side

explanation.surface: Fans chant furiously as their team takes the field.
explanation.definitionFit: Steaming is British slang for fuming, livid with rage.

clue.text: Celebratory church event not opening? It is opening

indicators.note: not opening means the first letter of the church word is dropped

parts.note: an agape is an early Christian love feast

explanation.surface: A church festival that doesn't open? It is, actually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening' appears twice: first it tells you to drop the first letter, then it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A gape is a wide opening, such as an open mouth or a gap.

clue.text: French writer's home flooded by water channel

indicators.note: flooded by means surrounded by water, so home sits inside the channel word

parts.note: a race is a channel of water, such as a millrace
in means at home

explanation.surface: A French author's house is swamped by a millstream.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean Racine was a 17th-century French dramatist, author of Phèdre.

clue.text: Name former US President as bringer of victory

parts.note: Ike was the nickname of Dwight D. Eisenhower

explanation.surface: Hail an ex-president as a triumphant hero.
explanation.definitionFit: Nike was the Greek goddess of victory, who brought triumph.

clue.text: Grave is end, leading to start of eternity?

parts.note: to sever is to cut off, put an end to

indicators.note: start of means the first letter of the word eternity

explanation.surface: Is the grave an end that leads into eternity?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grave' looks like a burial place but is an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Grave means serious or harsh, as in a severe illness.

clue.text: Security devices, out of date, sent back in bundles

indicators.note: in means the reversed date word goes inside the bundles word

parts.note: packs are bundles

indicators.note: sent back means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: old means out of date

explanation.surface: Outdated locks are returned packaged.
explanation.definitionFit: Detachable locks with a shackle, used to fasten gates and lockers.
